subject: Next Steps — POC Scope, Metrics & Owners (HorizonTech)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jaya Singh <j.singh@horizontech.com>, ops-team@horizontech.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Next Steps — POC Scope, Metrics & Owners (HorizonTech)

Hi Jaya / HorizonTech Ops team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the candid feedback and the use-case detail around ticket triage and automated summaries. Per our conversation, I wanted to document a concise POC proposal so we can align on scope, success criteria, timeline and owners.

POC objective (4 weeks, configurable):
- Validate Redwood Inference as the low-latency, production-grade inference path for HorizonTech ticket summarization and intent routing.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail + metric targets):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end response time < 400 ms for 10–20 concurrent requests.
- Quality: Human acceptance of autogenerated summaries >= 90% on the provided 250-item blind set (measured by 3 reviewers).
- Throughput: sustained throughput of 50 req/s without SLA breaches.
- Cost target: unit inference cost under $1.50 per 1k tokens (benchmark run to confirm).
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate over the trial window.

High-level evaluation plan:
- Week 0 (kickoff): technical onboarding, credentials, sample dataset transfer (SFTP/Drive).
- Week 1: ingestion + integration – API wiring, schema mapping, secure ingestion.
- Week 2: run evaluation harness + baseline metrics on 250 sample tickets.
- Week 3: tuning and quantization/throughput optimization, enable prefix caching where useful.
- Week 4: capstone run + joint review and next-steps decision.

Owners & roles:
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead), Karthik (solutions engineer) — contact for infra/quant/perf tuning.
- HorizonTech: Jaya (project sponsor), Sanjay (CTO, escalation), Emily (platform lead, integration owner).

Requests / open items for HorizonTech:
1) Confirm the sample dataset transfer method (SFTP or Drive) and data residency constraints.
2) Confirm acceptance criteria owners and reviewers for the quality evaluation.
3) Any corporate compliance requirements beyond SOC 2 we should be aware of.

I attached a short POC outline (PDF) with the same plan and a checklist of technical pre-reqs. If the timeline looks good, can we lock a 60–90 minute kickoff slot next week? I proposed three options in the attachment and below.

Proposed kickoff slots (PDT):
- Wed 5/19 10:00–11:30
- Thu 5/20 09:00–10:30
- Fri 5/21 14:00–15:30

Thanks — happy to shorten/extend the POC duration if you want an additional stability week.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Next Steps — POC Scope, Metrics & Owners (HorizonTech)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap and the outline. Quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Sample size — the 250-item blind set sounds fine as a baseline, but our platform will generate ~10k tickets/day. For throughput/latency testing we'd like to see a scaled run at ~5k items to ensure behavior under load. Is that doable within the POC?

2) Latency target — our internal SLA for user-facing tooling is stricter; can we aim for p95 < 300 ms instead of 400? If caching helps here, we'd be keen to understand the tradeoffs.

3) Compliance — we require SOC 2 and a short summary of controls (particularly around key management and retention). Do you have a one-pager we can share with legal?

Also looping Emily to coordinate ingestion and Sanjay for any architecture-level questions. Emily — can you confirm who on your team will provision access?

Available kickoff windows: Thu 5/20 morning works for us.

Best,
Jaya
Director, Platform & Ops
HorizonTech
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jaya Singh <j.singh@horizontech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps — POC Scope, Metrics & Owners (HorizonTech)

Thanks Jaya — great questions. Short answers inline and next steps below.

1) Scaled run: yes — we can accommodate a 5k-item load test in the tuning week. Our standard approach is a two-stage run: baseline on the 250 blind set, then a load run with synthetic concurrency to emulate 5k/day traffic (we'll provide a runner harness). If you prefer a real-data run, we can coordinate a redacted export.

2) Latency: p95 < 300 ms — realistic on dedicated capacity with optimized batching and prefix caching. We'll propose a config that targets that and include a fall-back profile if you want to trade a small quality delta for latency. Karthik, can you prepare the initial perf config for the kickoff?

3) Compliance: attaching a SOC 2 summary and short KMS note — this should satisfy legal for an initial review. For the POC we can provide encrypted transport and customer-managed keys if needed.

Kickoff: Thu 5/20 09:00 PDT works from our side. Let's lock 60–75 minutes: 09:00–10:15 PDT to leave time for integration questions. Agenda: 1) Introductions & roles, 2) credentials and network checklist, 3) data ingestion approach, 4) perf targets & load plan, 5) reporting.

Prep items for HorizonTech before kickoff:
- Provide sample dataset (anonymized) or confirm synthetic runner approach.
- Provide list of reviewers for the quality acceptance run.
- Confirm any network/VPN or firewall rules for the agents we'll call from the POC harness.

We'll bring: kickoff deck, perf harness, SOC2 summary, short RBAC/KMS doc and a DocuSign for the POC access agreement (if you want formal access controls).

Thanks — looking forward.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf

Marissa — thanks, that all looks good. Confirming kickoff Thu 5/20 09:00–10:15 PDT. Emily will provision an SFTP share and loop in our infra engineer (vinay.patel@horizontech.com) for firewall rules.

Two small updates from us:
- We agree to the baseline plan but would like to extend the POC by one extra week (5-week total) to allow for a production-like run after tuning.
- Sanjay asked that the quality acceptance include at least one cross-functional reviewer outside of platform (e.g., product manager) — we'll share the reviewer list before kickoff.

I've added a shared folder link here for the sample data and reviewers list: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cHorizonTech_PoC_Drive

See you on the call.

Best,
Jaya
